cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and what falls, falls cleanly.
cells.act: refine one piece by repeating it
cells.ask: Go back to a piece of work you have already done and do it once more today, exactly as it was, adding nothing. Let the repetition itself show you what is underneath it.
cells.core:
Something gives way and you are present for it. A structure that couldn't hold lets go, and you don't rush to put up another one in its place. You know the difference between a break and a clearing, and you let the clearing be a clearing. The space stays open because you don't hurry to fill it.

There is a small practice you keep steady on, and it holds you because you do it whether it feels useful or not. Stay with it this week. Take one part of it and do that part again, the plain way, and let completing it be enough. This quiet time is not distance from anyone. It is where your real attention lives. The clearing stays clear when something underneath it is being kept lit.
cells.sheetLine: You can let what falls fall, and keep your small practice.
cells.verb: clearing away what can no longer hold

cells.tense: You will be standing in the rubble of something you tore down before it was ready.
cells.act: hand one thing on in the way you were handed it
cells.ask: Show someone a skill or practice exactly as it was shown to you, keeping the form intact. Allow one change only if it makes the thing truer, and say why.
cells.core:
You are not clearing anymore, you are shattering. Every structure looks false to you, so nothing gets to stand long enough to be tested. It feels like speed, like freedom. It reads as chaos from the outside, and from inside it is draining.

Something needs to be carried forward instead of torn down. There is a practice you inherited — a way of doing something, a ritual or a skill that was handed to you. Pass one piece of it on this week, in the shape you received it, with one honest change. Teaching what you have already received will slow you down in the right way, and put a floor under you where there wasn't one.
cells.sheetLine: You're tearing down the walls before you've checked the foundation.
cells.verb: clearing away what can no longer hold

cells.tense: You were keeping upright something that had already gone, and your arms are still holding it.
cells.act: give the mess a shape it can be carried in
cells.ask: Name what you keep propping up though it has stopped working, and give it a boundary. A final task, a last conversation. Where it ends is yours to set.
cells.core:
You have been bracing against something that already happened. The old forms are gone and you are still underneath them, keeping them up, and that is where your energy goes. Not denial exactly — loyalty to something that no longer fits.

Potential does not need you to let go; it needs a container. Give the mess a shape you can carry. Take the dead structure and put a limit on it: a last day, a last conversation, a final task that ends it. You are not killing it, you are giving it a grave instead of a load. What you build now starts with this small boundary, and the boundary is the beginning of something that can actually hold.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding up something that already fell, and it's wearing you down.
cells.verb: clearing away what can no longer hold

cells.tense: The pen is down, but the writing is already happening in the room.
cells.act: move toward the thing you want, one step, today
cells.ask: Do something small toward what you want, before you feel ready. No announcement, no plan behind it.
cells.core:
You are steering without noticing your hands are on the wheel. Things are shifting around you — a job, a role, a way of being — and you keep filing it under circumstance. Some of those shifts are your own doing. Nothing has your name on it yet.

The want is already there under the surface. Breakthrough comes from genuine insight, and insight starts as a pull, a direction you haven't named yet. Move toward it once today, one step, before you feel ready. It doesn't need to be big, and it doesn't need a reason. The step itself is the recognition, and it will tell you more than another week of waiting to feel certain.
cells.sheetLine: You're already moving, you just haven't claimed the direction.
cells.verb: clearing away what can no longer hold

attempts.check: The record supports Breakthrough as a sudden clearing of structures that couldn't hold, seated in Potential (the seed state, everything possible, nothing chosen). The unsupported claim I make in Too Much is that the person is causing the shattering — the record says premature shattering, chaos disguised as liberation, unable to let anything stand; I read this as something they are doing to themselves, but the reader could reasonably say it is simply happening around them. In Too Little I claim they are holding up what has already stopped holding; the record supports clinging to dead structures, but the reader could say the structures are not dead, just slow. The ask survives being wrong either way: the Discipline act is small, private, repeatable, and teaches something even if my read of the situation is wrong. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'the collapse isn't coming, it's already here' — I have cut it. Too Much and Too Little are opposite failures of one capacity: one cannot let anything stand, the other stands under what has already fallen.
